title: Emergency Credential Delegation — runbook + audit mapping
content:
Purpose:
Provide an operator-friendly runbook for emergency credential delegation (temporary privilege elevation / break-glass) and a clear mapping of audit fields to the SIEM and evidence automation pipeline. This document is intended for on-call SREs, security engineers, and incident commanders when standard credential issuance is not possible or too slow.

Scope / When to use:
- Use when a single user or service requires immediate short-lived access to a production secret (DB root, KMS unwrap key, service account impersonation) to mitigate a P0 incident.
- NOT for routine maintenance or planned access; those must go through the standard request workflows (CLA/IT ticket + approval + scheduled rotation).

High-level constraints and guarantees:
- Delegated credentials must be ephemeral (TTL <= 1 hour by default) and recorded as evidence with signature.
- Delegation must be approved by at least one on-call security lead OR incident commander (Slack approval recorded).
- RBAC v2 role escalation is auditable: every step must produce an audit event with event_id and evidence_id.
- SIEM export must contain the raw audit event and a normalized summary for dashboards.

Trigger checklist (operator):
1) Confirm incident qualifies for emergency delegation (incident commander sign-off).
2) Post approval in #sec-ops with explicit text approval (example: "@seclead approve emergency delegation for user:alice -> db-admin for 45m") so Slack can be ingested by the evidence collector.
3) Run the delegation flow below (or ask SRE with vault-admin scope).

Delegation flow (step-by-step):
1. Create a delegation request record (CLI): secctl delegate create --requestor alice --target-role db-admin --reason "restore-replica" --ttl 45m
   - CLI returns request_id. Copy request_id to Slack approval message.
2. Approval: Incident commander OR on-call security lead must reply in thread with "approve <request_id>". Evidence collector will scrape thread and attach the approval.
3. Vault issuance flow (automated if possible):
   - Exchange: Operator runs secctl delegate approve --request <request_id>. This triggers Vault (namespace:prod/emergency) to issue a short-lived credential.
   - Implementation detail: The vault path uses an emergency mount with special policy: policy:emergency-delegate-v1 which allows issuance only after an approval event anchored to request_id.
4. Post-issue hardening steps:
   - Immediately restrict network access to the token if possible (e.g., K8s service account annotation + pod-level NetworkPolicy).
   - Start a focused audit trace: trace_id = tracing.start("emergency-delegate", request_id) and annotate every related action with trace_id.
5. Revoke/Rotation: After TTL expiration, the credential must be revoked automatically. If operators revoke early, they must run secctl delegate revoke --request <request_id>.

RBAC v2 considerations (short):
- Role escalation is recorded in the new RBAC v2 events: role_grant_request, role_grant_approved, role_grant_issued, role_grant_revoked. Each event must include: actor, requestor, approver, target_role, request_id, ttl_seconds, resource_scope, and evidence_id.
- Mappings: short-lived delegated credentials map to existing model of service accounts but with 'delegated:true' flag in metadata so downstream tooling treats them differently (no caching, stricter rate-limits).

Audit schema (canonical event fields) — REQUIRED for every step:
- event_id: unique-uuid-v4
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- event_type: one of [delegation_request, delegation_approval, delegation_issue, delegation_revoke, delegation_expire, action_using_delegation]
- request_id: human-friendly id created at request time
- actor: principal that performed this event (user/service)
- approver: principal who approved (if applicable)
- target_role: canonical role name (e.g., db-admin, kms-unwrap)
- resource: canonical resource path (e.g., k8s/cluster-prod/namespace/payments/secret/db-root)
- ttl_seconds: integer (if applicable)
- trace_id: optional tracing correlation id
- evidence_id: pointer to stored evidence bundle (S3 path or internal id)
- signature: base64 signature of the event payload (for later non-repudiation)

Example audit event (single-line JSON for clarity):
{
  "event_id":"e6f3a8d2-4c2b-4f1a-9f3b-2a5d9f77b0e1",
  "timestamp":"2024-05-09T14:22:31Z",
  "event_type":"delegation_issue",
  "request_id":"del-20240509-87a1",
  "actor":"vault-admin@redwood.com",
  "approver":"seclead-maya@redwood.com",
  "target_role":"db-admin",
  "resource":"rds/prod/payments/db-root",
  "ttl_seconds":"2700",
  "trace_id":"trace-9b8f",
  "evidence_id":"evidence/S3/2024/05/09/del-20240509-87a1.json",
  "signature":"MEUCIQDn...base64..."
}

SIEM export mapping (summary):
- Splunk sourcetype: redwood:secrets:delegation.audit (raw event is full JSON)
- Elastic index: redwood-secrets-audit-YYYY.MM
- Normalized fields added by the forwarder: red_event_type, red_actor, red_request_id, red_role, red_evidence_id, red_ttl, red_trace_id, red_sig_verification (OK|FAIL)

Sample Splunk query (investigation):
index=redwood-secrets-audit red_event_type=delegation_issue target_role=db-admin | stats count by red_actor, red_request_id | sort -count

Evidence automation pipeline (how evidence is collected and stored):
- Slack approvals -> evidence-collector lambda (sec-evidence-collector) -> signs message with KMS key -> stores JSON bundle to s3://redwood-evidence/prod/<date>/<request_id>.json. The bundle contains: request, approval messages, audit events, signature, operator notes.
- Airflow DAG (dag_id=sec_evidence_reconcile) runs every 5 minutes to ensure every open delegation has a corresponding evidence bundle. Missing bundles trigger PagerDuty to on-call security.
- For higher assurance (customer-required): evidence bundle is copied to secure-archive (S3 with different KMS + retention policy) and a hash is stored in internal ledger (DB encrypted with HSM-wrapped key).

Operator checklist (post-issue):
- Confirm evidence bundle exists and signature verifies: secctl evidence verify --evidence-id <id>
- Annotate incident in PagerDuty with request_id and evidence_id
- Keep the delegation trace active: add any manual actions to the trace (tracing.append)
- After remediation, revoke or let TTL expire and then run full reconciliation (secctl delegate reconcile --since <incident-start>)

Retention / compliance notes:
- Evidence bundles for emergency delegations are retained for 7 years by default for legal/regulatory use (configurable per customer).
- Audit logs are forwarded to SIEM and retained according to security retention policy (default 2 years in hot index, 5 years in cold archive).

Post-incident reconciliation (required steps):
1) Incident commander and sec lead review the evidence bundle and approve post-mortem notes.
2) Update RBAC mappings if the delegation exposed a policy gap (issue a follow-up Jira ticket: SEC-XXXXX).
3) Rotate any long-lived credentials that may have been indirectly exposed (check the reconciliation script output).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we reduce human approval friction by allowing automated approvals for low-scope delegations (e.g., read-only DB queries)? (security lead + product sign-off required)
- Add a cryptographically stronger envelope for Slack approvals (challenge: signing rapid messages).
- Confirm whether Splunk will accept the full signed payload or only normalized fields; update forwarder accordingly.

Appendices:
A) Helpful commands (CLI):
- secctl delegate create --requestor <user> --target-role <role> --reason "<why>" --ttl 45m
- secctl delegate approve --request <request_id>
- secctl delegate revoke --request <request_id>
- secctl evidence verify --evidence-id <evidence_id>

B) Relevant tickets / docs:
- Confluence: SEC/credential-delegation (design doc for emergency mount)
- Jira: SEC-4123 (implement evidence-collector lambda), SEC-4210 (airflow reconcile DAG)
- GitHub: infra/ops#456 (vault emergency mount config)

C) Quick contacts:
- On-call security lead: #sec-oncall (Slack)
- SRE emergency pager: PagerDuty (team: infra-sre)

Notes to self (rough):
- Consider schema versioning in the audit payload (field: schema_version) for future RBAC v3 changes.
- We currently sign with KMS; plan to test HSM-backed signing for high-assurance customers.

End of runbook.
